paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: nobody out-plots God. The kings of the earth lined up to break the chains, and the One enthroned in heaven laughs. Then He tells them, "I have installed My King on Zion, upon My holy mountain." (Psalm 2:4, 6) Their plan was never even close to working, and that's the good news for everybody who's ever felt like the world is in a rage.

Now, this psalm doesn't leave it at laughing. It tells the kings to "be wise" and to "Serve the LORD with fear, and rejoice with trembling." (Psalm 2:10-11) Fear and joy in the same breath? That's the cookie batch coming out of the oven, friend: you're thrilled AND you're holding the mitts with both hands. Bowing to the LORD's Son isn't a loss. It's the wisest move on the whole planet.

And watch how the psalm ends, because it's the whole point. After all that warning, it says, "Blessed are all who take refuge in Him." (Psalm 2:12) Same Son, same power, and one open door. So when the headlines get loud and everybody's typing in all caps, you know where to run, baker: straight to Him.
